history.period: Samvat 1307 (1250 CE) to Samvat 1698 (1641 CE) - built across four generations
history.summary: The Keshav Rai Temple stands on the banks of the Chambal River at Keshoraipatan in Bundi district. Legend says Lord Vishnu appeared to Raja Ranti Deo as two idols - white-stone Keshavji and black-stone Charbhuja Nath; Ranti Deo began the temple in Samvat 1307 (1250 CE), and the work proceeded in fits and starts over four generations until Rao Raja Chattar Salji of Bundi completed it in Samvat 1698 (1641 CE). The white-stone Keshav Rai idol sits in padmasana holding discus and conch, wearing a vaijayantimala; the shikhara over the sanctum rises in four carved storeys to a kalash while the jagmohan shikhara is round, with Rajasthani-style canopies on the two-storey outer portion. The campus also holds a Shiva shrine of Jambu Margeshwar, traditionally founded by Rishi Parashurama (legend - verify). Worship originally followed the Ramanuja Sampradaya and later Pushtimargiya practice; priesthood is hereditary. Believers hold that the Chambal takes a U-turn after touching the Lord's feet. Keshoraipatan also has a notable Jain temple of Munisuvrata nearby (separate site - verify). town_description: Keshoraipatan is one of the oldest towns in Bundi district, Rajasthan, on the banks of the Chambal River, about 45 km from Bundi city and 20 km from Kota. It is known for the Keshav Rai Temple where the river is said to bend around the shrine, and also hosts a noted Jain temple of Munisuvrata.
